candidates.description: Smelt raw ore batch 1 in the primary furnace, turning it into ingot batch 1.
Smelt raw ore batch 2 in the second furnace, turning it into ingot batch 2.
Forge ingot batch 1 at the anvil into a finished ingot. Only becomes legal after ore/raw1 has been ordinarily smelted into ingot/batch1 -- tempering the primary furnace instead forecloses this path.

Quench the primary furnace's raw ore batch 1 with the catalyst instead of smelting it normally, spawning a tempered furnace that produces a finer ingot. Retires the primary furnace's own smelt (its ore stock is consumed) and forecloses the ordinary forge-ingot1 path, since the anvil only ever checks for ore/raw1 refined the ordinary way.

spawns_followup.description: Fire the tempered furnace's own superSmelt on the ore the catalyst transferred to it, producing a marked fine-quality ingot instead of an ordinary one.

candidates.description: Quench the second furnace's raw ore batch 2 with the catalyst instead of smelting it normally, spawning a tempered furnace that produces a finer ingot. Retires the second furnace's own smelt (its ore stock is consumed); does not affect the ordinary forge-ingot1 path, which only ever depends on ore/raw1.

spawns_followup.description: Fire the tempered furnace's own superSmelt on the ore the catalyst transferred to it, producing a marked fine-quality ingot instead of an ordinary one.

jev.instructions: Given the actions legal this round in a small crafting world, choose the one that seems most interesting or valuable to pursue -- there is no single objectively correct path. Ordinary smelting is reliable and simple; tempering is a one-time-only capability (only one catalyst exists) that trades away a furnace's normal output for a finer one, at the cost of foreclosing whatever depended on that furnace's ordinary path.
